narrative_critique.headline: Terraced Spine on the Slope
narrative_critique.concept_statement: A circulation spine threaded through terraced concrete-and-glass volumes that step with the hillside, using the path as the organising datum from which stacked platforms descend. The parti reads as a sectional descent — movement and topography are made coincident.

category_critiques.concept_originality: The terraced-spine parti is legible and competently composed (edge_ratio 0.032, 76 lines), but it stays within a familiar hillside-pavilion idiom rather than pushing a singular idea — a justified 6.
category_critiques.spatial_hierarchy: The strongest move: 76 dominant lines (48 vertical, 28 horizontal) register a clear circulation armature and stepped datum, and per circulation_and_spatial_order.md the path genuinely organises the plan rather than sitting as leftover space — a deserved 7.
category_critiques.transparency_light: Despite the concrete-and-glass ambition, brightness 0.62 with a white ratio of 0.00 reads as opaque; the glazing is asserted but not yet luminous, leaving the daylight argument unconvincing at 4.
category_critiques.materiality_detailing: Colour variety 0.166 and saturation 0.07 around a single grey #a59f93 give a monolithic but undifferentiated surface; per materiality_and_tectonics.md the finish risks being decorative rather than tectonic, with no expression of how the concrete and glass actually meet — 4.
category_critiques.alignment_keywords: Terraced massing and the spine come through, but concrete-and-glass transparency is under-expressed (keyword expression 0.46, RAG similarity 0.47), so the image only half-delivers its own brief — a fair 5.

strengths: Legible circulation spine as organising armature
Strong open-space ratio reading the slope
weaknesses: Glazing reads opaque, not luminous (white ratio 0.00)
No visible tectonic joint between concrete and glass
recommendations: Render night or section views to prove the glass as a transparent membrane, not a grey plane
Articulate the concrete-glass junction — reveal, mullion rhythm, or poche — to make the tectonics visible
Differentiate the terraces materially (texture, board-marking) so the section reads as stacked rooms, not one mass
Let the spine resolve into a threshold or terminus event rather than a uniform path
narrative_critique.justification: The 5.2 overall is fair: the project earns its highest marks where circulation_and_spatial_order.md is satisfied — the spine acts as a true armature (spatial_hierarchy 7) — but is dragged down by materiality_and_tectonics.md, against which the flat grey palette (saturation 0.07) appears decorative rather than tectonic (materiality 4) and the glazing fails its own transparency premise (white ratio 0.00, transparency 4). A competent, legible parti that has not yet made its concrete-and-glass tectonics or daylight convincing.
